::: {.home-section .home-hero}
# We map the wild alleles that helped maize adapt, and put them to work in modern maize.

The Genetics, Evolution and Metabolism of Maize Adaptation Lab combines quantitative
and population genetics, lipidomics and gene editing to study cold tolerance and
nitrogen and phosphorus efficiency.
:::

::: {.home-section}

## Research tracks

::: {.tracks}
::: {.track}
[Local adaptation]{.track-name}

How teosinte *mexicana* introgressions such as *Inv4m* and the phospholipase *HPC1*
changed flowering time and lipid metabolism in highland maize.
:::

::: {.track}
[Nitrogen and N₂O]{.track-name}

NSave Maize, with ARPA-E: nitrification-suppressing and nitrogen-recycling alleles
from wild relatives, to cut nitrous oxide emissions.
:::

::: {.track}
[Cold tolerance]{.track-name}

CERCA: highland alleles lost during domestication, like those in Palomero Toluqueño,
so maize can be planted earlier.
:::

::: {.track}
[Phosphorus]{.track-name}

With the NSF STEPS center: phosphorus use efficiency in maize and sorghum, and gene
edits that lower phytate in the grain.
:::

::: {.track}
[Lipidomics]{.track-name}

Population-scale lipid profiles of maize and sorghum, open as the
[Sorghum Lipid Database](https://nirwan.shinyapps.io/SAP-Lipidomics-Database/) and the
*Zea Lip* leaf atlas.
:::

::: {.track}
[Teosinte introgressions]{.track-name}

ZeaL, the Zea Exotic Allele Library: 82 teosinte accessions crossed into B73, plus
2,208 near-isogenic lines in CML311, to find wild alleles worth keeping.
:::
:::
